ns1:item.dc:creator: Patricia Rodriguez Dorribo Ramón Alberto Díaz-Varela Department of Botany, Escola Politécnica Superior de Enxeñaría, Campus Terra, Universidade de Santiago de Compostela, Lugo, SpainPatricia Rodriguez Dorribo is a Forest Engineer with a master’s degree in Unmanned Aerial Systems and Geographic Information Systems (2023). She is currently a predoctoral researcher in Biodiversity and Natural Environment Conservation at the University of Santiago de Compostela (Botany Department, Campus Terra). Her doctoral work focuses on the methodological development and application of emerging remote sensing tools—including UAV‑based sensing, LiDAR, hyperspectral data and GIS workflows—to quantify forest structural attributes and improve ecological indicators in agroforestry and protected ecosystems. She works on testing and validating these methods in real conservation and land management projects, with the aim of strengthening monitoring practices, supporting decision making, and facilitating mechanisms for long-term ecosystem conservation and financing. Her research interests include biodiversity assessment, carbon dynamics, land use change, the integration of remote sensing metrics into conservation and biodiversity credit frameworks, and their transfer to practical conservation contexts.Ramón Alberto Díaz-Varela is a Forestry Engineer (1999), and European PhD from the University of Santiago de Compostela, awarded the Extraordinary Doctoral Prize (2005). He is currently an Associate Professor (Profesor Titular) in the Department of Botany at the Polytechnic School of Engineering and a researcher in the BioAplic group of the University of Santiago de Compostela, specializing in the application of remote sensing and geographic information systems to biodiversity characterization, modeling and monitoring, as well as the environmental applications of remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS). He is also coordinator of the Forest Engineering Master at the University of Santiago of Compostela. Research experience includes stays at leading institutions in Norway, the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain, as well as a period as a level 30 postdoctoral researcher at the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission (2012–2013). He has authored 41 journal articles, 19 book chapters, 6 books, and over 60 conference contributions. He also serves as a member of the editorial board for the JCR-indexed journals Remote Sensing and Forests, and acts as a reviewer for several leading international publications in remote sensing, ecology, and forest sciences.Since 1996, he has participated in or coordinated six European, nine national, and thirteen regional research projects, together with more than 50 R&D contracts. Furthermore, he has supervised four doctoral theses, with a fifth one currently in progress.
